turns.content: In carbon tetrachloride, what intermediate normally forms when bromine adds to an alkene, and what stereochemical outcome follows? Also note that an alkoxy group can stabilize adjacent carbocationic or oxocarbenium-like charge by resonance donation.
2-Methoxybut-2-ene instead gives both cis and trans dihalides on bromination. What does that product mixture say about whether the usual pathway operates exclusively?
How can the methoxy substituent stabilize an open positive intermediate, and why would that intermediate allow attack from either face?
Use this comparison to explain the loss of stereospecificity in the reaction.
How confidently can the open-cation pathway be assigned from the product pattern alone, given that no trapping, kinetic, or substituent-series evidence is available?
What stereochemistry would an exclusively bridged bromonium pathway predict, and why does that counterfactual favor the open intermediate here?
Summarize the proposed mechanism and the electronic role of the methoxy group.
